text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic talks with his Danish counterpart and chairman of the OSCE Niels Helveg Petersen in Copenhagen on promotion of bilateral relations and normalisation of Yugoslavia's relations with the EU.
- Taxi drivers reach agreement with Serbian government, halt strike. Import tax for taxi drivers to be reduced to 14 percent from 64.
- Novi Sad bus factory Neobus and Germany's Mercedes Benz sign an agreement on joint production of tourist buses.

- Greek trade delegation visiting Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce. Greek-Yugoslav trade stood at $250 million last year, at $30 million in the first two months this year and is planned to reach $400 million this year.
- Serbian textile and leather producers ask for import of 5,000 tonnes of material worth $18 million.
- Summer flight schedule will be applied from March 30; nine foreign airlines to land at Belgrade airport in the summer period.
- Main board of Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro has concluded there is no alternative to Yugoslavia.
- Coordinator of Montenegrin free trade zone project resigns; criticises new law on off-shore companies.
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade city assembly adopts 1997 budget at 1.5 billion dinars. Belgrade mayor Zoran Djindjic says the budget can only cover functioning of the city and not bigger investments.
- Elections for student parliament to be held today.
- The Serbian information ministry soon to submit a second working version of the new information law.
- Speculation about a rift within the Bosnian Serb leadership is propaganda aimed at destabilising the Serb entity says Serb representative in the Bosnian Presidency Momcilo Krajisnik.
- Belgrade Archbishop France Perko addresses Easter greetings to Roman Catholics.
- Round table on Kosovo will be held from April 7-9 in New York, organisers said.
BORBA
- Yugoslav-Danish joint venture confectionary factory set up in Osecina near Valjevo.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Mercedes Benz to open modern show room and service in Belgrade together with Serbia's Inex Interexport.
- Public District prosecutor in Pristina to charge 15 Kosovo Albanians for crimes committed in the period from 1992 to 1996.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Taxi drivers and private truck drivers block traffic in central Belgrade Wednesday, public transport at a standstill.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic in his statement Tuesday hints on who the next president of Yugoslavia will be by saying his party will support Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic if he is nominated for the post.

- New central bank building under construction irritates owners of frozen hard currency savings accounts, but bank claims it is being built with funds collected during former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

- War invalids from 1990 demand settlement of their status. Serbian government owes benefits for ten months. Around 2,892 families of war invalids and 1,100 families of killed receiving benefits in Serbia.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin airlines to start flying in mid-April.
- Port of Bar has achieved 30 percent better results this year than the previous year.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic to unveil monument to WWI Montenegrin General Janko Vukotic on Friday, April 28.
- Two hundred refugees from Albania who landed by boat in Ulcinj instead of Italy two days ago returned to Albania.
- For Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic there are only two options - a federal state with Slobodan Milosevic or no federal state at all, says Novak Kilibarda, president of the People's Party.
MONITOR
- The main board of Democratic Party of socialiststs supported (Serbian President) Slobdan Milosevic's policy, TV Serbia explains the substance of the problem, editorial.
- Milosevic is the creator of tension - interview with Ratko Knezevic, Montenegrin trade representative in Washington.
- Why Vukasin Maras, the head of the security service, was not acceptable to Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.

- All key positions in the federal parliament are taken by Milosevic's men for special purposes (Milan Milutinovic, Zoran Sokolovic, Vladan Kutlesic, Nikola Sainovic, Nedeljko Sipovac). -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
